title: JRE 2288 - Jacques Vallée

recap:
Joe brings on Jacques Vallée, one of the most respected researchers in the field of unidentified aerial phenomena, to discuss his extensive work documenting and investigating UFO sightings over several decades. Vallée is primarily promoting his new book Forbidden Science 6: Scattered Castles, which contains his personal journals from 2010 to 2019. Throughout the conversation, Joe and Jacques dive deep into what makes UFO research such a compelling and frustrating field to work in.

Vallée explains that his approach to studying UAPs has always been grounded in scientific methodology despite the stigma attached to the subject. He developed a classification system early in his career that helped organize different types of sightings, moving beyond the simplistic idea that everything falls into either extraterrestrial or misidentified aircraft categories. The conversation touches on why governments have maintained such strict secrecy around these phenomena for so long, and how institutional resistance continues to prevent serious scientific investigation. Vallée points out that the reluctance to study UAPs isn't necessarily about protecting classified military technology but something deeper about institutional protection and academic credibility concerns.

Joe and Jacques discuss specific cases Vallée has investigated, including encounters with credible witnesses such as military pilots and scientists who have direct experience with anomalous phenomena. What makes these accounts compelling is the quality of witnesses and their professional standing, yet mainstream science continues to dismiss the field. Vallée emphasizes that the real mystery isn't necessarily aliens but understanding what these phenomena are and what they represent about our reality. The conversation explores how technology advancement might help us understand these experiences better, and Vallée reflects on his dual careers as both a researcher and venture capitalist investing in technology companies. The episode covers everything from consciousness and physics to government bureaucracy and why some of the most important questions remain unanswered.
